_doc: Acknowledged reds — vibe-ic#1025. Adjudicated by
vibe-ic-marketplace/plugins/vibe-ic/programs/gate_red_since_check.py.
A row here grants NO leniency. The hygiene suite still exits 1 for every
FAIL exactly as it did before this file existed, so there is nothing a row
can silence and no green a row can buy. The ONLY thing a row does is start
a clock that gate_red_since_check will fail on once `max_commits` is
exceeded. Adding a row is therefore taking on a deadline, never escaping
one.
Delete the row in the SAME commit that fixes the gate. A row that outlives
its truth is failed as `stale`, because a stale acknowledgement is
indistinguishable to the next reader from a live one, and it is the row
that gets believed.
FIELDS
gate         the gate's label EXACTLY as tools/ci/_gate_dispatch.sh
records it. A label that matches nothing in the record is
failed as `stale`, so a drifting label cannot go quiet.
since        the commit at which the gate went red — the ANCHOR of the
row's age, and the thing renewal moves.
since_date   that commit's own date, ISO-8601 WITH an offset. Required,
and checked against the commit `since` names: a row whose
stated date contradicts its own anchor is failed as
`misdated`, so a row cannot misreport its age to a reader.
Re-dating it buys nothing in any case — the clock reads the
repository, not this field.
max_days     how many DAYS this red may survive before this file fails
the landing gate. Required — an acknowledgement with no
bound never comes due, which is the state being removed.
IT WAS `max_commits`, AND A COMMIT COUNT WAS THE WRONG CLOCK
(measured 2026-08-22). The age was `rev-list --count
<since>..<head>`, which is a property of the MERGE TOPOLOGY:
on a 97-branch assembly every merged branch's commits fall
inside that range, so the rows below read 1590-2109 against
bounds of 140-210 and every one would have been called
EXPIRED — by an assembly none of their authors had anything
to do with. `--first-parent` was not the repair: several
`since` shas are not on the head's first-parent chain, so it
would have silently mis-aged exactly those. How stale a
promise is, is a property of when it was made.
STILL NOT WALL TIME. The age is measured to the ENDPOINT'S
commit date (`--head-ref`, the BASE for a landing), so two
readers of the same tree still compute the same answer and a
candidate still cannot move its own clock.
max_commits  how many commits this red may survive before this file
fails the landing gate. Required — an acknowledgement with
no bound never comes due, which is the state being removed.
owner        the issue or PR that will close it.
why          why it is red, in one sentence, for the reader who finds
this file six weeks from now.
adjudicated  present when a ruling has been written down for this row: the
verdict and where to read it. A row carrying one is NOT to be
renewed by moving `since` forward -- the ruling replaced the
question the deadline was asking.
bound_because why max_commits is THAT number and not a larger one. Not read
by the adjudicator -- read by the reviewer, who is the only
defence against a bound chosen for comfort. A bound whose
reason is 'so the board stays green' is the thing this file
exists to catch.

acknowledged.why: floorplan_hints, power_budget_uw and sdc_constraints_path are read by a checker and populated in 0 of the 4 documents that carry them, so the consumer cannot tell empty from clean.
acknowledged.bound_because: The fix is in vibeic/benchmark-data, not in this repo: either the L-docs populate the three fields or the checker declares them optional, and a cross-repository change needs a round trip. 210 commits is three days at the measured rate. It is the longest bound here and it is still 290 short of the ceiling. || SUPERSEDED 2026-08-22, kept because it was true when measured: the corpus moved (b971220) and now holds NO L-doc carrying a `fields` object at all, so the fix described above — populate the three fields, or declare them optional — is no longer the question. The gate returns rc 2 UNDETERMINED over a zero denominator, which is correct behaviour; what is wrong is the DISPATCH recording rc 2 as FAIL. The bound is not what needs revisiting here. || CLOCK MIGRATED 2026-08-22, bound UNCHANGED: the deadline is a DURATION now, because a commit count is a property of the merge topology — a 97-branch assembly put this row at 2111 commits against a bound of 210, which is the assembly's shape and not this row's age. max_days is this row's OWN figure, carried over unrounded: “210 commits is three days at the measured rate”. It is neither extended nor shortened; if it has passed, it has passed.
acknowledged.adjudicated: REAL FINDING — stays red until fixed, NOT renewed. docs/research/2026-08-21-corpus-gate-adjudication.md

acknowledged.why: Went red at ec43bba14 ('an rc 2 that named the artefact it READ, not the one it awaits') — MEASURED by single-step bisection: rc 2 at its parent d9a55b005, rc 1 at ec43bba14. The gate now separates two questions it used to fold together: 54 of 91 records in ppa-crosslayer/records/trials/b000/records_flat.json are REFUSED, and those findings do NOT depend on a denominator. Coverage itself stays UNDETERMINED for want of an `expected` list. THE REPAIR IS RE-PRODUCING THE RECORDS, NOT FIXING CODE, and an earlier version of this row said the opposite. MEASURED: all 54 refused records carry source.parser_sha256 sha256:054a956d923c110d53b6fd5..., while the shipped _ppa/backends/opensta.py hashes to sha256:f9dd6f34dc8850b4949d326... Both defects the refusals name are ALREADY FIXED upstream of these bytes: the 26 SAME_ARTEFACT_TWO_VALUES rows have no path_startpoint/path_endpoint/path_ordinal in scope, which _ppa/timing.py has emitted since v1.11.33 precisely so several paths in one (clock, check) view stop colliding; and the 30 scope.clock=null rows come from before timing.py grew the `p.clock is None: continue` guard it now carries. The records predate their own producer. This closes when trials/b000 is re-produced with the current backend, not when anybody edits a program.
acknowledged.bound_because: MEASURED cadence ~78 commits/day, so 200 commits is ~2.6 days. THE BOUND IS LEFT WHERE IT WAS EVEN THOUGH THE REASONING BEHIND IT WAS WRONG. It was first justified as 'code, not a re-measurement'; the repair is in fact a re-measurement, which is the more expensive job, so the honest instinct is to lengthen the clock. That instinct is exactly what 'never extend a bound' forbids, and extending it here would be an author widening his own deadline using his own corrected reasoning. 200 stands. If it expires before trials/b000 is re-produced, that is a conversation the gatekeeper should be forced to have, which is what an expiring clock is for. || CLOCK MIGRATED 2026-08-22, bound UNCHANGED: the deadline is a DURATION now, because a commit count is a property of the merge topology — a 97-branch assembly put this row at 1594 commits against a bound of 200, which is the assembly's shape and not this row's age. max_days is this row's OWN figure, carried over unrounded: “200 commits is ~2.6 days”. It is neither extended nor shortened; if it has passed, it has passed.
